title: Arizona Public Service Company 2023 Integrated Resource Plan (Public)
doc_type: Integrated Resource Plan (filed with ACC under A.A.C. R14-2-703)
summary: APS's most recent filed IRP (30 MB, ~525 pp.), covering 2023-2038. The Preferred Plan adds nearly 8,000 MW in the 2023-2027 Action Plan window and more than double that over 15 years: hydrogen-capable gas CTs, New Mexico wind via repurposed Four Corners transmission, >2 GW batteries (cap 3 GW through 2027), Cholla retirement by April 2025, Four Corners exit 2031. Peak demand grows from 8,184 MW (2023) to 13,119 MW (2038); energy grows 23,689 GWh led by data centers (12,997 GWh). Lists 2023-2032 Ten-Year Plan transmission projects. ACC acknowledged the plan Oct 8, 2024 (per the 10-Q).

findings.location: Attachment F.1(a)(9), p.247 (PDF p.258); F.9(b)(1) p.288

findings.statement: Base peak growth ~2.4%/yr after DSM/DER, ~3,400 MW (230 MW/yr) over 15 years; low case 0.9%/yr (~1,200 MW).
Energy growth 2023-2038 total 23,689 GWh: new data centers 12,997, large industrial 5,843, EVs 3,406, C&I 785, residential 657 GWh; data centers add ~1,550 MW peak, large industrial ~690 MW.

Preferred Plan future resources (accredited MW at peak) 2027 / 2031 / 2038: natural gas 201 / 1,302 / 3,034 (CT 199/1,302/1,587; CC 0/0/1,446 from 2035); wind 270 / 494 / 789; PVS (PV+BESS) 1,885 / 1,958 / 2,156; energy storage 644 / 923 / 1,174; microgrid 544 / 742 / 767; total future resources 3,584 / 5,602 / 8,155.

Existing coal accredited 1,347 MW (2023) drops to 970 (2025, Cholla retired) and 828 (2026-2030), then 0 from 2031 (Four Corners exit); existing natural gas falls from 5,832 MW (2023) to 2,875 MW (2038) as tolling agreements expire.
Existing resources ~13,397 MW nameplate: nuclear 1,146 (Palo Verde), coal 1,357 (Four Corners 970, Cholla 387), natural gas 5,216, storage 300, renewables 1,448, customer-based 3,888.

Preferred Plan replaces Four Corners in 2031 with wind firmed by gas using the existing Four Corners transmission path; nearly 8,000 MW of new resources in the 2023-2027 Action Plan, with more than 2 GW batteries and a 3 GW battery cap through 2027; 2023 ASRFP sought >=1,000 MW (700 MW renewable).
findings.location: Executive Summary pp.5-11; Ch.5 p.81; Ch.6 pp.85-86

findings.statement: 2023-2032 Ten-Year Plan: ~29 mi new 500 kV, 1 mi new 345 kV, 54 mi new 230 kV, 11.5 mi underground 230 kV, 40 mi 230 kV rebuilds, 3 mi 115 kV upgrades, 27 new transformers; projects include Panda-Freedom 230 kV rebuild (2025-2027), Jojoba-Rudd 500 kV (2025-2028), Sun Valley-TS23 230 kV (2026-2027).
Transmission contracts for New Mexico resources on non-APS systems are not expected available until 2031; new company-owned transmission investments not forecast in service until 2036.
